summary: The state cuts aid to towns in the middle of the year and towns freeze hiring, plan layoffs and warn of tax rises.
realLife: Connecticut cut about $50 million of aid to schools and towns at the end of December 2016, mid-year. In October 2017, with no state budget, an executive order cut more than $900 million in municipal aid; Southington faced a cut of 14 percent of its annual budget and froze hiring, Litchfield warned of an 8 percent tax rise, and New Haven froze hiring for positions outside public safety and canceled a youth work program.
